proposition: Six of the letters in the Munshaʾāt-i Turka (nos. 4, 10, 21, 22, 23, 27) are addressed to Amīr Jalāl al-Dīn Fīrūzshāh, whom MK, following Manz, calls the greatest patron of the religious establishment (Sufis included) among Shāhrukh's amirs; Fīrūzshāh was the principal amir Ibn Turka wrote to.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, writing to Amīr Fīrūzshāh
mediation.note: Letters to third parties ask or offer favours; the text survives only in copies made after his lifetime (except the marginal letters in MS Majlis 10196).

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, summarising, dating and identifying the letter(s)
mediation.note: The identification of the addressee of letter 4 is 'almost certain' per MK
